spans.label: Accessors: height, get_leaf (past the frontier returns V::empty_leaf), get_root, leaves, len, is_empty
spans.note: get_leaf silently returns the empty leaf for every index at or beyond the frontier, so a caller cannot tell an unfilled slot from one holding the empty leaf. Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement.

spans.label: IncrementalMerkleTree::update(index, leaf): rewrites an existing position; `self.leaves[index]` panics past the frontier
spans.note: The Rust out-of-bounds case is a panic and, worse, it happens AFTER merkle_tree.update_leaf has already mutated the backing tree; the Except model returns an error and leaves the tree untouched, so that intermediate state is not modelled. Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement.

spans.label: IncrementalMerkleTree::push(leaf): index = len, assert!(index < 1 << height), hash, push, update_leaf
spans.note: The assert! is modelled as an Except error rather than a panic. The append increments the count by one, leaves every earlier leaf and the cached ladder untouched, and sets the root to the path recomputation from the new leaf and the pre-append frontier siblings. Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement.

spans.label: IncrementalMerkleTree::prove(index): wraps MerkleTree::prove
spans.note: prove is total: it also answers for indices at or beyond the frontier, returning cached empty-subtree hashes. Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement.

spans.label: Closing brace, blank line, derive and serde attributes
IncrementalMerkleProof newtype over MerkleProof plus the dummy / get_root / verify / from_siblings delegations
spans.note: Every method is a one-line delegation whose semantics lives in merkle_tree.rs; the local re-model implements the delegated fold and root comparison and its agreement with the real MerkleProof is not proved. Verification is a hash comparison: it implies membership only under collision resistance, which constant_hash_forges_membership shows is genuinely required. Note this proof type is `pub MerkleProof<V>`, so callers can build one from arbitrary siblings.

boundaries.name: backing-merkle-tree-remodel
boundaries.obligation: MTree/BitPath/updateUp/proveLoop are a handwritten local re-model of the private MerkleTree and BitPath of src/utils/trees/merkle_tree.rs and src/utils/trees/bit_path.rs. That the re-model agrees with those files (and with the separate Zkp.Implementation.MerkleTrees module, which is deliberately not imported) is not proved.

boundaries.name: hash-collision-resistance
boundaries.obligation: The hash is an opaque callback. Nothing here says a verifying proof implies the leaf was appended, that the root after an append differs from the root before it, or that two different leaf sequences have different roots. Those need collision resistance of the concrete Poseidon instance; constant_hash_forges_membership exhibits a callback under which they fail.

boundaries.name: leafable-trait
boundaries.obligation: V::empty_leaf(), Leafable::hash and LeafableHasher::two_to_one are arbitrary functions here. No property of the concrete instances, and no agreement between native and in-circuit hashing, is assumed or proved.

boundaries.name: u64-index-arithmetic
boundaries.obligation: Indices and BitPath::value are u64 in Rust and Nat here; push's bound `1u64 << height` is modelled as 2^height with no shift overflow, and BitPath::sibling's `value ^= 1` is modelled as an arithmetic low-bit flip.

boundaries.name: panics
boundaries.obligation: push's assert! and update's Vec index are process panics in Rust, modelled here as Except errors. In particular Rust's update mutates the backing merkle tree before the index panic, leaving a tree whose root no longer matches its leaves; that partially-mutated state is not modelled.

boundaries.name: serde-roundtrip
boundaries.obligation: The Serialize/Deserialize impls are not modelled; nothing rules out a packed tree whose stored height cannot hold its stored leaves (Rust would panic on unpack).

boundaries.name: circuit-targets
boundaries.obligation: IncrementalMerkleProofTarget and the plonky2 CircuitBuilder lowering are not modelled. No theorem here constrains an arbitrary satisfying in-circuit witness, and native/target agreement is not proved.

boundaries.name: frontier-consistency-across-history
boundaries.obligation: Only single-step facts are proved (one push, one update). That an arbitrary sequence of pushes and updates keeps every stored node equal to the hash of its children -- so that prove(i) for any i < len always verifies -- is not proved, and its use as an inclusion argument would additionally need collision resistance.
